_meta.what_this_is: One log stream from a service handling three requests (r1, r2, r3) concurrently. Each request follows the same path -- start, query, done -- and because the requests run at the same time their log lines interleave in the stream. Each event carries a correlation id (the request it belongs to); the 'without id' view drops it. The question is whether you can reconstruct any single request's path from the log: by filtering on the correlation id, or by naively chunking the id-stripped stream into groups.
_meta.data_is: A FIXTURE. The events are hand-authored so the interleaving defeats naive chunking (the stream is start,start,start,query,query,query,done,done,done, so no group of three is a valid start-query-done path) while correlation-id filtering recovers all three exact paths. Every reconstruction is computed in trace.py.
_meta.format: expected_path: the step sequence a real request follows; events: [{t, id, step}] where t is the timestamp, id the correlation id, step the stage.
